problem_type: KIE Kling 3 Omni model and input-field drift
symptom: KIE Kling 3 mappings sent the historical kling-3.0/video model and legacy mode, sound, and multi_shots fields instead of the current documented text-to-video and image-to-video contracts.
direct_cause: The shared KIE Kling operation was retained after the provider split the model identifier by mode and renamed the audio and multi-shot controls, while the generated archetype defaults were treated as the provider wire contract.
class_root: KIE provider-specific model identity and field ownership were not enforced at the KIE Kling operation boundary, so both modes could inherit stale generic defaults while local construction remained type-valid.
affected_population: Existing projects routed through the kling-3.0 archetype
entry_points: The shared KIE Kling create operation used by both mappings

external_sources.purpose: Defines the text-to-video model ID and current audio and multi-shot input fields.
Defines the image-to-video model ID, image_urls cardinality, auto aspect ratio, and current audio and multi-shot input fields.

invariants: KIE Kling text-to-video always sends model kling-3.0-omni/text-to-video.
KIE Kling image-to-video always sends model kling-3.0-omni/image-to-video and an ordered image_urls slot.
Both modes send only documented Kling input names; single-shot mode sends customize_multi_shots=false and prefer_multi_shots=false, with no multi_prompt.
Image-to-video single-shot mode sends aspect_ratio=auto because the official page restricts fixed ratios to custom multi-shot mode.
generality_proof: Both KIE Kling modes converge on the same catalog boundary and were affected by the same stale operation. A mode-specific shared factory now owns the provider model identity and the complete documented field projection, preventing either entry point from inheriting the other mode's contract.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Build the mode-specific KIE Kling Omni model and documented input shape for both mappings.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The official text-to-video page specifies kling-3.0-omni/text-to-video and customize_multi_shots, prefer_multi_shots, audio, resolution, aspect_ratio, and duration.
The official image-to-video page specifies kling-3.0-omni/image-to-video, exactly one or two image_urls, auto aspect ratio for non-custom shots, and the same current control names.
Seedance uses a separate official model/input contract and remains covered by the all-mapping dry-run; no Kling legacy field is shared with its operation.

recurrence.reason: Provider model IDs and field names can change independently of generic archetype defaults, and both KIE Kling modes inherited the same stale operation.
same_class_scan: Searched all KIE catalog operations for multi_shots, customize_multi_shots, prefer_multi_shots, mode, sound, and Kling model literals.
Compared all 32 KIE mappings in the zero-network vendorDocAuditWire suite; only the two Kling mappings had the affected legacy field family.
Checked APIMart Kling separately; it uses a different endpoint and audio contract and is not routed through the KIE operation.

prevention.invariant: The only KIE Kling create operations are mode-specific factories that emit the current official model and field names.
prevention.failure_mode: A regression in either mode's model or field projection fails the structural contract test before network use.
prevention.strategy: Keep provider-specific ownership in one small KIE factory and remove the stale shared operation rather than adding a compatibility fallback.

legacy_paths.rationale: The stale shared operation was deleted; both mappings now use the mode-specific current-contract operations with no fallback.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The drift is in the provider HTTP contract, not a dependency runtime.

migration: Persisted model identity remains kling-3.0 for routing compatibility; only the outgoing KIE model and input fields are corrected at the request boundary.
residual_risks: KIE's current docs still conflict with previously accepted live response, callback-domain, and URL-expiry behavior; those remain explicitly double-sourced in the audit report and are not changed by this request-body fix.
The UI's historical mode control remains available in the shared archetype, but KIE no longer emits it because the current official Kling page does not define it.
